Give yourself time to park and get up to the rooftop. There is paid parking near The Radical entrance, street parking nearby, and additional parking down below behind The Radical. For that lower back lot, put Bull & Beggar in your GPS.

Or take a Lyft and skip the parking question entirely.

A Little About Asheville

Before we get to all my recommendations, a little context will help.

Asheville is a small city tucked into the Blue Ridge Mountains with deep Appalachian roots, and its neighborhoods feel very different from one another.

First, look up while you're here. The mountains show up from rooftops, while you're driving, along the river and sometimes at a stoplight. Take a minute.

Hurricane Helene hit Western North Carolina in September 2024. Two years later, you'll still see reminders, especially along the French Broad River, in the River Arts District and Biltmore Village. Asheville is open and very happy to have you. You may see empty lots, construction or places that haven't returned. Supporting local businesses while you're here genuinely matters.

Downtown

Compact, historic, quirky and very walkable. Grove Arcade, Pack Square, Battery Park Book Exchange, Pritchard Park, shops, restaurants and rooftops.

Park and start walking. Go into the shop. Stop when you hear music. Find a rooftop. Change your mind about dinner.

Getting around
Drive or Lyft downtown, then walk. The hills are real.

River Arts District

The Radical puts you here for the wedding, but daytime RAD is completely different: old industrial buildings, working artist studios, galleries, murals and the French Broad River Greenway.

Helene hit this area hard and the food/beer scene is still rebuilding and changing. Wedge is a solid local brewery stop; Golden Hour and Bull & Beggar are strong dinner options.

Getting around
Drive/Lyft to a cluster, then walk. Don't walk here from downtown just because your phone says it's technically possible.

West Asheville

Haywood Road, coffee, restaurants, breweries, vintage, records, neighborhood bars and old houses. Funkier, less polished and very local.

You're here Saturday night for The Low Down. Come back when it's light out too.

Getting around
Haywood is long. Pick a section and wander.

Biltmore Village

A distinct historic neighborhood, not the Biltmore Estate. Developed around Vanderbilt's estate, it has distinctive architecture, shops, galleries, restaurants and coffee.

Helene recovery is still visible, but businesses are back and it deserves more than a drive-through on the way to Biltmore.

Getting around
Drive/Lyft, park, then walk the Village.
Shellie's transportation note: I have much better luck with Lyft than Uber in Asheville. Walk within an area. Drive or Lyft between them. Asheville looks compact on a map until a hill, bridge or disappearing sidewalk enters the conversation.

🐻 A Note About Our Bears 🐻

Early October is still very much bear season in Asheville, and yes, you may see one wandering through a neighborhood or even close to downtown. Black bears live here. They aren't visiting.

Enjoy the sight from a distance, never approach or feed one, and definitely don't position yourself between a mama and her cubs. If you're driving, keep an eye out too.

Around here, “bear traffic” is an actual thing.

Explore Asheville

Have a free morning, afternoon or an extra day? Pick the version of Asheville that sounds good to you.

Wedding-day reality check: The ceremony begins Saturday at 4:30 PM. Don't plan a six-hour adventure Saturday and discover at 4:05 that you're supposed to be dressed and on a rooftop. Save the bigger excursions for Friday, Sunday or an extra day.
⛰ I want mountains

Blue Ridge Parkway: drive, stop at overlooks, get out of the car and look around. You don't even have to hike. Check current road conditions before you go and whatever you do, do not feed the bears!

North Carolina Arboretum: gardens, wooded trails and nature without requiring hiking boots and a hydration strategy.

Low-effort plan: coffee + Parkway + two overlooks + back into Asheville for lunch. You saw the mountains and still have functioning legs.

🛍 I want to wander, shop + eat things

♥ Couple Favorite Asheville City Market: Saturday morning producer-only farmers market with local produce, bread, pastries, cheese, meat and prepared foods. Go hungry.

Grove Arcade: local shops, galleries and food. Inside you'll also find ♥ Couple Favorite Enter the Earth for crystals, minerals, fossils, gems and jewelry.

Battery Park Book Exchange: books + champagne. Enough said.

♥ Couple Favorite Ignite Jewelry Studios: beginner-friendly jewelry/metalsmithing workshops. If you want to make something instead of buying a souvenir, check the schedule and book ahead.

🎨 I want art + something that feels like Asheville

Go back to the River Arts District. Attending a rooftop wedding at The Radical does not mean you've seen the RAD.

Pick a cluster and wander into working studios. Painters, potters, jewelers, glass artists, photographers and people making things I don't know how to categorize. Walk part of the French Broad River Greenway, stop at Wedge, and buy something directly from an artist if you fall in love with it.

🌀 I want a very West Asheville day

Start at Rowan West, Cooperative Coffee or BattleCat. Or ignore coffee and go straight to ★ Taco Billy for breakfast tacos.

Walk a section of Haywood Road. Have lunch at Hail Mary, Haywood Common or Gypsy Queen. Stop at Archetype if a beer sounds good.

Then find ♥ Couple Favorite Fleetwood's. Vintage shop. Bar. Music. Wedding chapel. I've explained this as much as it can reasonably be explained.

🌿 I want wellness + a reset

♥ Couple Favorite Asheville Yoga Center: a longtime Asheville yoga institution with drop-in classes and a wide variety of styles.

♥ Couple Favorite Hot Yoga Asheville: heated flow, Hot 26, Yin and strength-based classes. Bring water. Obviously.

♥ Couple Favorite Skinny Beats Sound Shop: part world-instrument shop, part sound-healing space. Check the schedule for sound meditation and other experiences.

♥ Couple Favorite Asheville Salt Cave: a quiet, immersive salt-cave experience with zero-gravity chairs and a definite “we are in Asheville now” feeling. Reservations are a good idea on a weekend.

🏰 I want to do the Biltmore
IMPORTANT: PLAN THIS IN ADVANCE.

If you want to enter Biltmore House, reservations are required every day. You choose a specific House entry time when purchasing your ticket. Biltmore recommends booking at least 7 days ahead for preferred availability and pricing. Do not assume you can decide that morning and walk in.

Biltmore Tickets

And give it time. The House is only part of the Estate. There are gardens, trails, restaurants, Antler Hill Village, the winery and views all over the property. If Biltmore matters to you, make it one of the main activities of a free day.

Saturday warning: with a 4:30 PM wedding, I would not make Saturday your full Biltmore day.

🍷 I want Biltmore Village without spending the day at the Estate

This is its own historic neighborhood and a lovely way to spend part of a day.

Brunch at Corner Kitchen. Walk the Village. Coffee or gelato at Affogato. Lunch and wine outside at Finch Grocery. Dinner at Gemelli. If you're still there afterward, pop into the Grand Bohemian for one cocktail and the decor.

😴 I want Asheville, but I don't want to work that hard

Late brunch. Walk downtown. Go into whatever shops look interesting. Sit somewhere outside. Have a beer or glass of wine. Go back to your hotel. Take a nap. Get dressed for the wedding or dinner.

You do not get extra points for seeing everything. Asheville is better when you leave enough room for something you didn't know you were looking for.

Leave a Little Love

Before you go, leave Steven & Ashley something to take with them. A wish for their marriage. A favorite memory. Something that made you laugh this weekend. Advice they absolutely did not ask for. Whatever you want them to have after the celebration is over.

Your note will be sent privately to Steven & Ashley's wedding wishes collection.

A final Asheville rule

Look up. Talk to people. Buy something from the person who made it. Support the places that fought their way back after Helene. And leave a little room in the plan to get distracted.

Have a beautiful weekend in Asheville.

And, most importantly, celebrate Steven & Ashley.
